key_insight: Phase-engineered bismuth-based double perovskites BFCO and BMCO show visible-light absorption and photovoltaic potential as lead-free alternatives to halide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The measured band-edge positions and carrier properties provide direct design guidance for selecting transport layers and improving device stacks in lead-free solar cells.
method: Solution-deposited 350–450 nm BFCO and BMCO thin films were fabricated.
Optoelectronic properties were measured using UV-vis and ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy.
A BMCO-based FTO/SnO2/BMCO/Spiro-OMeTAD/Ag device was tested and numerically simulated.
evidence_signal: The films showed strong visible absorption (α ~10^4–10^5 cm⁻1), carrier densities around 10^17–10^20 cm⁻3, and the BMCO solar cell reached 3.56% power conversion efficiency.
watch_item: Mixed cation valences and deep-level defects may limit efficiency unless defect control and phase quality are carefully improved.
paper_title: Beyond lead halide perovskites: visible light photovoltaics with phase engineered bismuth-based oxide double-perovskites, Bi2MCrO6 (M = Fe, Mn)
